status: COMPLETE — 1v1 and 2v2 both fully specified and both simulated. Ready for a paper playtest, print layout and a digital build.

power_system.note: Power Values (5-90) are FULLY REMOVED. Any card art or CSV still showing numbers is legacy and must be reprinted. Resolution is Type-Based Counter only.

match.turn_limit_ruling: ACCEPTED_BY_DESIGNER — no turn limit. A match ends only on goals_to_win or END_MATCH. Mitigating factor: a player holding possession MUST play an attack card each turn, so stalling is not a legal strategy; the deadlock case requires a player to repeatedly hold no attack card at all. Watch total match length in the first playtest.

split_card_rule: A split card carries one attack face and one defense face. Playing either face discards the WHOLE card — you cannot keep the other half. This is the core cost of the game: every Pass you make burns an Interception you could have used.

ASSIST.note: On success, possession transfers to your PARTNER, who may then play GOAL. This is the only route to the Goal card.

GOAL.play_condition: 2v2 only. Playable ONLY immediately after your partner has played a successful ASSIST, which transfers possession to you. It cannot be played free-standing.

PENALTY.play_condition: Play it after the opponent has committed a Foul against you. It is a guaranteed goal.
PENALTY.note: CLOSED (Q3): sits in the draw deck like any other card and can be drawn into hand.

counters.note: The ONLY answer to Super Shot in the entire game. ACCEPTED_BY_DESIGNER: Super Shot is meant to be a rare finisher, not a duel. Only 2 copies exist, and because Block Save shares its physical card, an attacker holding one Super Shot leaves just one possible save in the deck — the defender's real chance of holding it is nearer 7% than 13%.

Functionally identical to Goal Keeper, and INTENTIONALLY so. ACCEPTED_BY_DESIGNER: Goal Keeper is trapped on a split card with Shot Goal, so extra keepers would mean extra shots. Block Shot is a FULL card, making it the only way to add shot-defense to the deck without adding attacking power. The duplication is deck maths, not redundancy.

Stops Pass and Assist only, without taking possession — so Interception does the same job strictly better. ACCEPTED_BY_DESIGNER: kept as-is. It is also disabled in Strategy mode. Watch in playtesting whether anyone plays it by choice rather than as a forced defense attempt; its most likely real use is as burn fodder for the mandatory-defense rule.
CLOSED (Q2): does not stop Super Shot, so 'Super Shot is answered by Block Save only' holds.
NOT universal. Foul cannot answer Shot Goal, Super Shot, Goal or Penalty (designer correction).
Resolves as a coin-flip review, not a normal duel. Reviews a Goal card, a Penalty, or an Offside call against you. See resolution.var.

CLOSED (Q14): Chain interrupts BUILD-UP only. It cannot be played against any goal-scoring card — Shot Goal, Super Shot, Goal or Penalty — because a scoring card may only be answered by the defenses assigned to it in this table. Chain covers the same ground as Interception and Tackle combined and takes possession, which would dominate them both; its balance is scarcity, at 2 copies against 15 Interceptions and 5 Tackles.

resolution.core: Each attack card is answered by a specific defense card. Correct card = attack cancelled. Any other card = attack succeeds.
resolution.mandatory_defense_attempt: The defender MUST play a card from hand as an attempt even with no valid counter. That card is discarded and the attack succeeds. This is what keeps both hands at 4 — it is a resource rule, not a combat rule.
resolution.chain_opening: LOCKED: any Attack card may open a chain. A Shot may be played as the first card of a possession.
resolution.passed_stage: If defense fails on a non-shot card, that stage is marked PASSED and control returns to the attacker to continue the chain. The defender never defends the same card twice.
resolution.shot_success: If defense fails on a shot-stage card, a goal is scored immediately and the chain closes.
resolution.turnover: If the attacker holds no playable Attack card, the chain is cancelled and possession passes to the opponent. No other penalty.
resolution.foul: FOUL stops an attack at the build-up stages only — Pass, Dribble, Assist. It cannot answer a shot (Shot Goal, Super Shot, Goal) or a Penalty. Its cost is inverted: possession goes back to the fouled ATTACKER, not to the defender who played it. And it exposes you: a fouled attacker holding a Penalty card can convert it into a goal.

penalty.trigger: CLOSED (Q3): the PENALTY card is played from hand by an attacker who has just been fouled.
penalty.effect: A guaranteed goal. No Shot card needed and no normal duel occurs.
penalty.counters: LOCKED (L1): both OWN_GOAL and VAR are valid objections.
resolution_order: 1. The fouled attacker plays PENALTY from hand.

2. CLOSED (Q4): the fouling side may answer with OWN_GOAL — the penalty is converted and the point is scored FOR the fouling side. Possession then returns to the attacker who conceded it, exactly as with a normal Own Goal.
3. Either way the resulting scoring event may be reviewed ONCE with VAR by the side it hurts.
4. Heads = event confirmed. Tails = event cancelled.
5. If neither card is held, the goal stands with no objection possible.
penalty.note: The old automatic 'foul inside the box' penalty no longer exists — Foul cannot answer a shot, so a penalty now always comes from the card.

resolution.own_goal: Played as a defense against a shot. It does not merely stop the attack, it converts it: the point is scored FOR the side that played Own Goal. Possession then returns to the ATTACKER, who restarts play — exactly like a real side kicking off after scoring against itself. One copy in the deck. Against a Penalty it behaves identically: the penalty converts and the fouling side takes the point. In 2v2 it needs no special restart rule: the rotation naturally resumes with the conceding side.

var.reviews: the last decision: a goal, a penalty, or an offside call
var.chooser: the player who played the VAR card calls heads or tails before the flip
var.limit: One VAR per event, ever. No appealing an appeal.

resolution.chain_card: Playable at any time, but ONLY by a player on the side that does NOT hold possession, and ONLY against a build-up card (Pass, Dribble, Assist). It cancels the running chain and takes possession immediately. It can never touch a scoring card.

reshuffle.ONE_V_ONE: Swap exactly 2 cards from your hand with 2 from the deck.
reshuffle.TWO_V_TWO: Either swap 2 with the deck, or trade 2-for-2 directly with your partner's hand. Both hands stay at 4.

resolution.end_match: Playable at any time with no mechanical precondition — deliberately a "رخامة" (troll) card. The match ends instantly and the higher score wins. CLOSED: if the scores are LEVEL when it is played, the win goes to the OPPONENT of the player who played it. So the card is never a free win — playing it while not ahead hands the match away. Draws are therefore impossible.
resolution.deck_refill: The deck never runs out. When it empties, shuffle the discard pile and keep drawing from it. A match therefore only ends on goals_to_win or END_MATCH.
resolution.assist: An attack card at pass stage, 2v2 only. If the defense fails to stop it, possession transfers to your PARTNER rather than staying with you — and that partner may then play GOAL. If the Assist is stopped, no Goal is possible from it.
resolution.counter_attack: STRATEGY mode only. A defender who breaks possession with cards still in hand from his draw plays them immediately as his own attack chain. The original attacker then defends against it, answering only the last card of the counter-chain.
resolution.after_a_goal: Universal rule: the side that CONCEDED restarts play. Scoring never hands you the ball back. This replaces the earlier card-specific possession clause on Own Goal, which is now just a special case of the same rule.

LUCK.defense_answers: every attack card in the chain, one by one
LUCK.feel: fast, no planning, the only decision is timing

STRATEGY.play_per_attack_action: exactly the number drawn, as one uninterrupted combo
STRATEGY.defense_answers: the LAST card of the attacking chain only — middle cards pass automatically.
STRATEGY.feel: more control, chance to build a full combo
STRATEGY.hand_growth: none — hand is fixed at 4 in both modes, permanently (designer ruling).
STRATEGY.combo_reward: ACCEPTED_BY_DESIGNER — none. The mode's value is agency and hand management, not a mechanical bonus.
STRATEGY.actual_function: For the ATTACKER the 1-3 draw is mainly a hand-churn tool. For the DEFENDER it is the heart of the mode: stop the attack and launch a counter-attack in the same turn.
defense_engine: The defender draws 1-3 and spends them IN ORDER against the last attack card.
Card 1 is an attempt to break possession. If it is not a valid counter, he tries card 2, then card 3.
The first card that IS a valid counter succeeds: the attack is cancelled and possession resolves per possession_after_successful_defense.
Any cards still unspent at that moment become his own attack chain, played immediately in the same turn — a counter-attack.
If ALL his drawn cards fail, the attack succeeds normally.

A counter-attack is only possible when the successful defense card actually grants possession (Interception, Tackle, Offside). Goal Keeper, Block Save and Block Shot are neutral, so they stop the attack but launch nothing.

Leftover cards that cannot be played as an attack (full defense cards such as Foul, Own Goal, Offside, VAR, Block) are BURNED to the discard pile. Hand size returns to 4 either way — card parity between sides is never allowed to drift. Split cards are not affected: a Goal Keeper card can always be played on its Shot Goal face.
STRATEGY.skill_expression: Card ORDER is now a real skill, and the draw size is a genuine trade-off: drawing 3 raises the chance of stopping the attack but shrinks the counter-attack, since every failed attempt eats a card that would have been part of it. And what you draw matters as much as how many: drawing into full defense cards mid-counter-attack burns them for nothing, so a hand heavy on Foul and Offside is a hand that should draw 1, not 3.
STRATEGY.accepted_risk: With the shot-last rule in place, simulation shows the shoot-on-sight and build-up policies win 50.6% vs 49.4% — the mode is balanced and build-up cards are genuinely required. The earlier concern about combos being dominated is resolved by this rule.
STRATEGY.chain_order_rule: CLOSED (Q13): within a chain played in one turn, a shot-stage card must be the LAST card. Build-up cards come first. A shot therefore always faces a defense and can never slip through as an undefended middle card. Playing a shot ends the chain immediately; any cards still undrawn-but-owed from the draw are burned, per the same rule as counter-attack leftovers. This does not conflict with "any Attack card may open a chain" — a single-card turn may still be a shot.

ONE_V_ONE.scoring: a successful shot-stage card scores directly
ONE_V_ONE.after_a_goal: CLOSED: the conceding player restarts. Same principle as 2v2 — scoring never keeps you on the attack.

TWO_V_TWO.scoring: CLOSED (Q5): two routes. (1) Any successful shot-stage card (Shot Goal, Super Shot, Penalty) scores directly, same as 1v1. (2) A partner plays ASSIST; if it survives, possession transfers to the other partner, who may then play GOAL. GOAL is not playable without that Assist.
TWO_V_TWO.defender_selection: CLOSED: the defender is the NEXT player in the fixed turn order, who is always an opponent because the order alternates teams (T1P1, T2P1, T1P2, T2P2). The attacker does not choose his defender, and the defending team does not choose who answers — it is whoever the rotation names.
TWO_V_TWO.possession_transfer: CLOSED: when a defender wins the ball (Interception, Tackle, Offside, Chain), possession goes to his PARTNER, who attacks next — never to the winner himself. Winning the ball is a pass to your teammate, exactly as in football, and it keeps both partners involved by alternating them.
TWO_V_TWO.turn_structure: The ATTACKER is named by possession; the DEFENDER is the next player in the fixed rotation after that attacker, who is always an opponent because the rotation alternates teams.
TWO_V_TWO.neutral_possession: CLOSED: after a neutral save (Goal Keeper, Block Save, Block Shot) the ball goes to the NEXT player in the rotation, who attacks if he holds an attack card. If he does not, it carries on to the next player in the rotation, and so on. The ball can therefore return to the attacking team — which is what makes it genuinely neutral, and what keeps a keeper save different from winning the ball outright.
TWO_V_TWO.turn_slots: The four players occupy a fixed repeating rotation: T1P1, T2P1, T1P2, T2P2. Every action consumes the actor's slot — DEFENDING costs you your turn exactly as attacking does. That is why the defender is simply the next slot in the rotation.
TWO_V_TWO.after_a_goal: CLOSED: after ANY goal, play resumes at the next slot in the rotation belonging to the CONCEDING team. A normal goal therefore restarts with the conceding side's other player (the one who just defended has spent his slot); an Own Goal restarts with the conceding side too, since the side that was attacking is the side scored against.
TWO_V_TWO.partner_communication: CLOSED: partners may talk freely but must NEVER name or describe a specific card. "Leave this one to me" is legal; "I have the keeper" is not. The opponents hear everything, so the hint itself is information — which is the point. Hands stay hidden from the partner, so a Reshuffle partner-trade is a calculated risk rather than a solved move.

removed_cards.reason: bound to the deleted Power System, no replacement
CLOSED (L10): cut for now. May return in a later expansion.

design_principles: Luck mode is the intended core experience; Strategy is the alternative, not the baseline.
Simplicity over complexity — every revision so far has cut, merged, or removed rather than added.
Card-count parity between sides is a permanent priority. Every mechanic must leave both hands equal.
The game must be fully playable with 2 players. 2v2 is an extension on the same base, not a separate game.
Super Shot is a deliberate exception to the duel structure: a rare card that simply wins. Its balance comes from scarcity (2 copies), not from counterplay.
Deliberate duplication is allowed when a split card blocks a quantity change: a full card can add defense without adding the attack printed on its back.
A card that scores may only ever be answered by the defenses named against it in the counter table. No universal card is allowed to bypass that.
